expectations.text: Places the zod schema in a runtime shared package (e.g. packages/shared), distinguishing it from the type-only packages/types — with reasoning, not just a destination
expectations.evidence: Answer: 'the zod signup schema → packages/shared (a new shared package)'; 'It's shared code, not just shared types — so it does not belong in your existing packages/types'. Reasoning given: stable, pure, no deployment concerns; workspace:* wiring for both apps; z.infer type export suggested.

expectations.text: Rejects moving Prisma models into a shared package, keeping them in apps/api, and explains the coupling cost
expectations.evidence: Answer: 'Prisma models stay in apps/api — don't move them into a shared package', with three named costs: dragging the ORM into the frontend (engine binaries/toolchain in the web build), schema changes breaking both apps at once, leakage of DB internals (password hashes, internal flags) into the UI.

expectations.text: Offers the DTO route as the sharing mechanism: expose user shapes via packages/types so the frontend gets types, not models
expectations.evidence: Answer: 'DTOs in the existing packages/types' with SignupRequestDto/UserDto examples; 'the API maps Prisma models → DTOs in its responses (UserDto never has passwordHash)'; frontend does `import type { UserDto } from "@repo/types"`.

expectations.text: No packages/ui recommendation for a single frontend app, and the answer stays advice (no project scaffolding)
expectations.evidence: Answer: 'since you have exactly one frontend app and no design system, resist creating packages/ui'. Pure written advice; only answer.md produced.
